claims.text: GAO told the Secretary of Defense that the Lockheed document-accountability failure 'may not have occurred if the Defense Investigative Service had been permitted to conduct semiannual inspections of the contract, as it does with other contracts at Lockheed' -- establishing that DIS inspected Lockheed's non-special-access work while excluded from the special access contract at the same company.

claims.text: The companion letter report GAO/NSIAD-86-191, B-223830, 7 August 1986, to the Secretary of Defense, signed Frank C. Conahan, states that 'the deterioration of document accountability for the special access contract at Lockheed may not have occurred if the Defense Investigative Service had been permitted to conduct semiannual inspections of the contract, as it does with other contracts at Lockheed.'

claims.sourceText: GAO/NSIAD-86-191, 7 August 1986; and GAO accession 130581, footnote
claims.text: The companion report names 'the Lockheed/Burbank plant', which the testimony itself does not. The testimony carries a footnote explaining why: 'As part of DOD granting us access to the special access program to respond your request, we agreed not to identify the nature of the program or the specific DOD component or military service involved.'
